book.title: Wool
book.author: Hugh Howey
book.subtitle: A claustrophobic dystopian novel of truth, survival and emotional resilience
book.description: Set in a decaying underground silo, this novel follows characters who confront authoritarian control, systemic secrets and the emotional cost of seeking truth in a sealed world. It blends gritty, immersive dystopian world-building with literary depth, focusing on grief, identity and the quiet rebellion of human will. Themes of isolation, leadership and psychological resilience drive its cross-genre appeal for upmarket dystopian and literary fiction readers.

audienceMatch.title: Audience Insights
audienceMatch.keyCharacteristics: The primary readership is adults aged roughly 25–45 with strong female skew, highly engaged with dystopian, literary sci-fi and grief-driven narratives. Readers are urban, college-educated, digitally active, and favour ebooks and paperbacks. They value moral complexity, psychological depth and speculative settings with emotional stakes. Secondary audiences aged 45–64 show strong interest in philosophical dystopias, ethical dilemmas and reflective, discussion-friendly fiction.

analysisOverview.title: Key Analytical Overview
analysisOverview.readership: Readers are predominantly adults who seek emotionally resonant speculative fiction that interrogates power, loss and identity. The primary group is highly engaged online, active in BookTok, Reddit and Goodreads spaces, and gravitates toward dystopias with literary tone. Secondary readers, older and more academic-leaning, favour philosophical dystopias and ethical exploration. Both segments prefer character-driven narratives with psychological realism and strong thematic undercurrents.
analysisOverview.classification: The book sits at the intersection of literary dystopian fiction and post-apocalyptic speculative storytelling, marked by tense, claustrophobic atmosphere and emotionally reflective narration. It aligns with upmarket dystopian works focused on moral truth, grief and systemic control rather than action spectacle. Competitive comparisons place it alongside Wool, Station Eleven, The Road and Never Let Me Go, but distinguished by tighter emotional focus and enclosed-world tension.
analysisOverview.personas: Core personas include introspective, analytically minded readers such as Alison Greene, who seeks emotionally intense, philosophically rich dystopias, and Daniel Reyes, a globally minded, tech-savvy reader who values cinematic pacing, systemic critique and emotionally grounded speculative worlds. These personas reflect the book’s dual appeal: literary depth for reflective readers and immersive, idea-rich tension for younger digital audiences.
analysisOverview.marketingGuidance: Marketing should foreground claustrophobia, emotional stakes and the psychological cost of truth-seeking. Trailer-style teasers, character-driven voiceovers, dark atmospheric visuals and slow-burn tension perform best in awareness stages. Consideration and conversion should lean on thematic hooks—grief, resilience, rebellion—plus influencer commentary, book club angles and video-led creatives. Best-fit regions include the UK, US, Canada and Australia, with emphasis on Meta, TikTok and YouTube placements.

positioning.title: Genre & Market Positioning
positioning.subtitle: Positioned as an upmarket dystopian literary novel with emotional and philosophical depth.
positioning.description: Silo: A Struggle for Survival in a Dystopian World is positioned within the literary dystopian and post-apocalyptic fiction space, appealing to readers who value character-driven narratives and philosophical explorations of power, identity, and survival. Although it integrates hallmark features of science fiction like advanced silo-based environments and authoritarian systems, its true strength lies in emotive storytelling and ethical dilemmas. This places it squarely within upmarket fiction, ideal for book clubs, crossover readers between literary and speculative fiction, and fans of high-stakes, deeply reflective narratives.

moodAndTone.title: Mood & Tone
moodAndTone.subtitle: Gritty, tense, and emotionally reflective
moodAndTone.description: The narrative tone of Silo is dark, urgent, and emotionally grounded, with a persistent mood of claustrophobia, fear, and despair, contrasted by fleeting moments of hope. Through introspective and observant prose, it guides readers through the isolation and emotional intensity of life within a decaying underground society. The voice is both descriptive and immersive, drawing readers into its layered psychological landscape, where the stakes are both individual and existential.

marketing.title: Marketing Strategy for SILO
marketing.subtitle: Building Global Awareness for a Claustrophobic Dystopian Fiction
marketing.objective: To position SILO as a compelling, emotionally driven dystopian thriller for global adult fiction audiences, using a multi-channel campaign to drive awareness, book club adoption, and eventual cross-media interest.
marketing.keyInsight: Readers are increasingly drawn to richly introspective, tense dystopian fiction that explores themes of identity, truth, and the psychological toll of survival. SILO uniquely speaks to this, offering both page-turning tension and profound emotional stakes.
howToUse: Use this strategy for the pre-launch, launch, and 3-month post-launch marketing effort.
Coordinate messaging and visuals across digital and traditional platforms consistently.
Focus paid media efforts on storytelling creatives and emotionally resonant messaging.
Prioritise digital-first engagement before scaling to book club outreach and event appearances.
Optimise social and video content for bingeability and emotional relatability.
primaryKPIs: Number of pre-orders within first 4 weeks
Amazon and Goodreads reviews and ratings
Engagement rates on social video (shares, comments)
Cost per click (CPC) and cost per acquisition (CPA) on ads

funnels.name: Awareness
funnels.description: Establish the emotional stakes and atmospheric claustrophobia of the world in SILO through trailer-style teasers, character voiceovers, and visual-heavy content.
funnels.formats: Video ads, reels, TikToks, dark-themed carousel posts, animated character quote cards
funnels.optimisation: Test multiple taglines and imagery to determine highest-performing combinations for eerie, survivalist tone.

funnels.name: Consideration
funnels.description: Engage readers with deeper thematic hooks—grief, identity, and resistance—as well as endorsements from influencers, critics, and early readers.
funnels.formats: Email newsletters, influencer reels, TikTok reactions, author Q&As, pull-quote graphics, Reddit AMA
funnels.optimisation: Retarget audiences who engaged with awareness content to promote sampling and free chapter download.

funnels.name: Conversion
funnels.description: Drive sales through offers, urgency marketing (limited-time signed copies), and partnerships with book clubs and sci-fi podcasts.
funnels.formats: Amazon ads, BookBub placements, countdown social posts, podcast ads, in-store POS displays
funnels.optimisation: Enable A/B testing of copy that emphasizes different emotional arcs (grief vs. uprising) to fine-tune conversion.

videoCreativeScripts.script:
[Darkness fades in. Echoing breathing. A drip of water. Zoom slowly on a scratched silo door.]
VOICEOVER (Juliette): I was told the surface was death. That to ask questions was to die. 
[Cut to flickering lights, running footsteps through rusted corridors.]
VOICEOVER: But death... was already inside.
[Montage: Juliette climbing, a body floating in water, a child crying, lovers separated at a steel door.]
TEXT: SILO. A dystopia buried in silence. Coming soon.
